rv.q: While Shit. Meet. Fan. isn’t all that persuasive, it delivers jolts of spiky humor and a cast of hardworking household names.
Not funny enough for straight-up comedy, populated with characters too thin for drama, and lacking a wicked sense of caricature, it struggles to find a consistent, coherent voice.
What might have been a searing examination of privilege and hypocrisy
The actors work together seamlessly to make some fundamentally unlikable characters entertaining enough to tolerate for a few hours, waiting for their well-deserved uppance to come.

cn.t: Robert O'Hara's star-studded adaptation of Perfect Strangers earns mixed reviews, with critics praising its scathing humor about privilege and masculinity but faulting its contrived premise and unlikable characters.
